text_blocks.snippet: The FDA has stated that N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) is excluded from the definition of a dietary supplement because it was first approved as a drug before it was marketed as a dietary supplement. However, the FDA is also considering a rulemaking process to potentially allow NAC in dietary supplements. Currently, the FDA is exercising enforcement discretion regarding the sale and distribution of NAC-containing products labeled as dietary supplements, as long as they are not otherwise in violation of the FD&C Act.
